How each one is actually drawn - region by region, and the layers it is built from - is on the coding tab.

About this gene

Imported from the magic-gene intake, 2026-09-08. The wing, its veins and its rim are the same mirrored spot field read three times, so the veins cannot run off the wing and the rim cannot come adrift from it. The source placed the wing at an explicit centre; a mirrored SPOTS field with the spacing set near the barrel's length is the addressable version of that, and it means WHERE it lands is down to the seed.

Crossing two of them

Finding one

About 1 in 1,136 wild horses is born showing this. That is the whole of the supply: catch one, or make one with the carrot below. Breeds set their own pools and a breed built around this gene will carry it far more often than the wild population does.

The file

common/src/main/resources/horsegenetics/genes/painted_lady_wing.json — a data-driven gene, not a Java class. It is listed in the index.json beside it and registered by Genes' class initialiser at startup.

What it paints

Each outcome, described the way the gene file describes it, and then the layers that draw it in the order they are painted. The prose is the part a reader checks a bake against; the list underneath is what the engine actually did.

Painted Lady Wingmark

The wing, its veins and its rim are all the same mirrored spot field, read three times - so the veins cannot run off the wing and the rim cannot come adrift from it. The rim is the wing with a smaller copy of itself subtracted, which is the same trick every rim in this mod uses.

  1. the wing itself — SPOTS, painted with TOWARD
  2. veins across it — SPOTS × CRACKLE inverted, painted with TOWARD
  3. and a dark rim round its edge — SPOTS × SPOTS inverted, painted with TOWARD

Painted Lady Wingmark, coloured

The same wing in a colour the line carries, still rimmed and veined in dark. Fully recessive.

  1. the wing itself — SPOTS, painted with TOWARD
  2. veins across it — SPOTS × CRACKLE inverted, painted with TOWARD
  3. and a dark rim round its edge — SPOTS × SPOTS inverted, painted with TOWARD

Wild type

No wingmark.
